refutations.argument: Step 3 stipulates that the first loser chooses. But in the case's own scenario (F2) every loser has lost, and a player who lost has left the game (CR 800.4 premise of the case itself: multiplayer games continue after players leave). 103.1 is a rule that requires 'the loser of the previous game' to make a choice. CR 800.4h already settles what happens when a rule requires a player who has left the game to make a choice: the next player in turn order makes it. So the Comprehensive Rules already assign this choice by turn order, and the stipulation (first loser chooses, with a tie-break by agreement or random) contradicts 800.4h and cannot be accepted as a gap-filler. At minimum the case never addresses 800.4h, which is the specific rule on choices owed by players who left.

source.excerpt: In a match of several games, the loser of the previous game chooses who takes the first turn.

steps.conclusion: 103.1 requires a loser of the previous game, a player who is no longer in the game in a multiplayer game that ended with other players remaining, to make the choice.

source.excerpt: If a rule requires a player who has left the game to make a choice, the next player in turn order makes that choice.

steps.conclusion: When 103.1 requires a player who has left the game to choose, the next player in turn order makes the choice, not the first loser, so the stipulation in C3 conflicts with 800.4h.
